script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for March 27. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Right now, without any effort from you, your heart is beating.  It's been beating since before you were born.  It will beat 35 million times this year.

Your heart beats about 100,000 times every day. That's 35 million times per year, 2.5 billion times in a lifetime. Each beat pumps blood through 60,000 miles of vessels. The heart never takes a break. The sinoatrial node—your heart's natural pacemaker—generates electrical impulses that trigger each heartbeat.  This is why a heart can beat in a dish or be transplanted.

Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: The most essential work often happens without conscious effort.  Your heart reminds us that reliability doesn't require attention, and that the most dependable things often go unnoticed until they fail.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Essential Appreciation - Thank What Never Stops.

Here's your activity: Your heart has beaten every moment of your life. Place your hand on your chest and feel it. Spend 30 seconds just appreciating this tireless worker. What other essential, reliable things in your life deserve this gratitude? This helps you appreciate systems that work reliably without attention.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about your heart never stops can be applied to essential appreciation - thank what never stops. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
